lens: Raycast/Arc keyboard-first launcher: floating command bar, instant drills, minimal chrome
name: Signal Console
one_liner: A dark, command-first call console: a centred ⌘K bar drives every action, a quiet coach rail whispers during live calls, and a browsable persona library feeds an AI persona wizard.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the Raycast/Arc lens: a centred ⌘K bar is the primary action surface, chrome is a 56px icon rail with no header bars, and drills are one Enter away. Changed it in one place: coaching cannot hide behind a command bar. Second Nature (Deal Coach), Hyperbound (Live Call Coaching) and Yoodli (moment playback) all surface coaching persistently, so the live coach gets a visible rail while ⌘K stays available. The library gets a browse grid because hundreds of personas do not work as palette results. Self-scores: A 8, B 7, C 7; D 5.6; E 5.3; F1 6 (crowded market, open-source core lowers acquisition cost); F2 7 (per-vertical persona packs and call-centre licences); F3 3 (worth building).

ui_stack.role: Engine for the ⌘K command bar and library filter palette

ui_stack.role: Dialog, Tabs, Toggle Group (Voice/Text), Slider (rubric weights), Tooltip (model provenance)

design_language.typography: Inter for all UI (14px body, 15px in the console). JetBrains Mono for timers, scores, timestamps and model IDs, with tabular numerals wherever a score appears. Sora is dropped except as an optional landing headline.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Hairline borders and surface steps (canvas, surface, raised) instead of drop shadows. 10px radius on controls, 14px on cards, pill chips. One soft glow only on the active coach cue.
design_language.motion: Command bar opens in 120ms (fade plus 0.98 to 1 scale). Whisper cues slide in beside the transcript line that triggered them over 200ms, dwell 6s, then fade. Score rings tween once on debrief. No looping animation during calls except a slow signal-ring pulse while the caller speaks. Reduced-motion removes all of it.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 16px for controls and 20px in the rail. Every command row shows its shortcut as a mono kbd chip. AI provenance uses a small spark glyph in the model colour.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark is the default. Light mode follows prefers-color-scheme and can be toggled from the ⌘K bar. Light values: canvas #F7F8FA, surface #FFFFFF, ink #0B0D12, signal text #0F766E. All colours are tokens on :root.

navigation_and_ia: Routes: / (landing), /library, /library/new (wizard), /practice/:scenario (briefing), /practice/live, /debrief/:id, /progress, /team, /settings/models. A 56px icon rail (Home, Library, Practice, Progress, Team) expands on hover. No top header bars; each page has one title line. ⌘K is global and holds every action: start a scenario, search personas, build or contribute a persona, copy a Codex prompt for a persona or rubric change. Chords: G then L for library, G then P for progress. Auth and access pages are a single centred card.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Coach is a separate, out-of-character model call that never speaks to the caller, so the persona rule stays intact. It streams typed events (cue, next_question, objection, step_progress, criterion_estimate), each carrying the ids of the transcript lines it refers to. Target: a cue within 2 seconds of the caller's turn ending; at most one whisper per 20 seconds; quiet, normal and heavy intensity. Live scores are labelled estimate and show no letter grade until the debrief. The debrief reuses the same evidence ids, so a live cue and the final verdict point at the same quote. Score D: 5.6. The design clears the baseline only if the event contract and latency ship; without them the console is a prettier chat.
persona_library_and_wizard: The library is data, not code: each persona and scenario is a validated YAML or JSON file in a personas folder, tagged with role, industry, difficulty, objection types and a rubric template. v1 target: about 400 personas across 12 industries and 8 roles, plus about 120 scenarios, all added through reviewed pull requests. The wizard uses one structured-output schema, so drafts validate before they render. It accepts job descriptions, product URLs, CRM notes, pasted calls and ICP fields; it redacts PII before any model call and blocks fetches to private-network URLs. Score E: 5.3. It meets the baseline only if the content and the wizard both ship; the design alone does not exceed it.
signature_moments: ⌘K is the whole app: every action, persona search, scenario start and contribution lives in one centred bar.
Whisper cues appear beside the exact caller line that triggered them, with the quote, so the rep sees why.
Every rubric score is a chip that jumps to the moment in the transcript and replays it.
Each AI output carries a provenance chip with the model ID and call cost, for example 'gpt-4.1-mini, schema-validated, 14 quotes verified'.
The persona wizard streams the draft in field by field, and each field links back to the sentence that produced it.
'Drill your weakest' turns the lowest criterion into a 90-second drill started from the debrief.
openai_fund_angle: Models are visible on purpose. Every AI surface carries a provenance chip with the model ID and call cost, and Settings, Models lists voice, coach, grader and wizard with per-session token spend. The voice path gets an OpenAI Realtime provider beside the current ElevenLabs path, so the default demo can run on OpenAI end to end; until that ships, the showcase claim is weaker. Contributors: a 'Contribute a persona' command runs the wizard and writes a validated file ready for a PR; a Good first persona board; an AGENTS.md so Codex CLI can add personas, rubrics and tests; and ⌘K commands that copy a ready-made Codex prompt. The README shows which OpenAI models are used and the cost per call.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0: tokens, shadcn primitives and the cmdk shell behind a flag; keep Tailwind 3.4 and map .card and .btn-primary onto the new classes. Phase 1: icon rail, ⌘K, landing page and README hero. Phase 2: live call console with the coach event contract, then the debrief. Phase 3: persona YAML schema and seed library, then the wizard. Phase 4: progress and manager views. Mobile pass in every phase. Retire the three.js orb from live screens only after the console ships. Add a voice provider abstraction before any OpenAI default.

risks: Whispers that arrive late or too often can wreck a call; ship with a throttle, an off switch and a visible latency gauge.
Live rubric estimates can discourage reps; label them as estimates and hide letter grades until the debrief.
400 personas is a content problem; without reviewer guidelines, generated personas can stereotype industries.
The wizard ingests URLs and CRM notes: SSRF and PII risk unless URL fetches are allowlisted and text is redacted before model calls.
When the grader fails, the debrief falls back to a keyword score; the amber fallback chip must stay conspicuous so it is not mistaken for a real grade.
Keyboard-first can hide features from mobile and screen-reader users; every ⌘K action needs a visible button.
If the default voice stays ElevenLabs, the OpenAI fund showcase is weak; the Realtime provider has to land.
Dark-first is a brand change the owner may reject; light tokens are defined as the fallback.
